# 🔢 The conductor of the order generated by characters of Sp(2m) at a torsion element — code and data

Companion material for *Where the character values of $\mathrm{Sp}(2m)$ at a torsion element fail to
generate the ring of integers* (Carles Marín), deposited on Zenodo:
[doi:10.5281/zenodo.22813216](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22813216). That is the **concept
DOI** — it always resolves to the current version — and it carries the note in both editions,
English (29 pp) and Spanish (30 pp), under Apache 2.0.

Both PDFs are here too — `conductor_rho_line.pdf` and `conductor_rho_line_es.pdf`, byte for byte the
files deposited on Zenodo — together with the code, the archived output, and the two LaTeX sources
with their figures, so that either edition also rebuilds from this directory alone.

This is **not** a fourth part of the series in the root of this repository. Those papers are about
Schur polynomials at a root-of-unity orbit, and `characters-at-aP/` is about character *values* on
Kostant's $\rho$-line; this note is about the **ring those values generate**, and what it is missing.
It lives here, rather than in a repository of its own, so that the material of one line of work is
found in one place.

## 🎯 What the note proves

Let $\xi=\xi_q$ be a primitive $q$-th root of unity and let $g=g_{1/q}$ have eigenvalues
$\xi^{\pm1},\dots,\xi^{\pm m}$, with $1\le m<q/2$. The character values generate an order
$A=A_m(q)\subseteq\mathcal{O}=\mathbb{Z}[\xi+\xi^{-1}]$, and the note locates and describes its
conductor. Write $h=2m$, $q=p^vq'$ with $p\nmid q'$ and $d=\varphi(q')/2$.

1. **Which primes.** Every prime of the index divides $q$; and for $q'\notin\{1,2,3,4,6\}$, a prime
   $p\mid q$ divides it **exactly when** $q'$ divides $h$, $h+1$ or $h+2$ — the three families of
   integer points at which $g$ is conjugate to all its prime-to-$q$ powers. The combinatorial input
   is a lemma on scales that also answers a question about musical tuning.

2. **What the defect looks like.** At each such prime the conductor is a power of the radical, the
   order has a single maximal ideal above $p$ with residue field $\mathbb{F}_p$, and the first graded
   layer has the dimension of the cyclic module over $\mathbb{F}_p[(\mathbb{Z}/q')^\times]$ generated
   by an explicit **first-moment function** of the segment $\{\pm1,\dots,\pm m\}$. Lengths, a
   Gorenstein criterion in layers and the Cohen–Macaulay type follow.

3. **Why class numbers appear.** That first moment is Stickelberger's sawtooth, or the same sawtooth
   shifted by half a period — and one identity, $2\hat s_n(c)=s_n(2c)-s_n(c)$, governs both regimes.
   The maximal minors of the moment matrix are Sinnott's index, so the conductor at $p$ is the
   radical **exactly when** $p\nmid h^-(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{q'}))$; a simple divisor of $h^-$ gives
   $\mathfrak{r}^2$ and a Gorenstein ring; on the shifted sawtooth the subgroup $\langle2\rangle$
   decides everything, with almost Gorenstein rings of type $2\delta-1$; and the index closes,
   $v_p([\mathcal{O}:A])=2d-1-W_1$, whenever the first layer is more than half full.

4. **Below and beyond.** When $p$ divides the multiplicity there is a **universal ladder** of layers
   at the degrees $P-p^j$, $P=p^{v_p(N)}$, whose first term is Kontsevich's finite logarithm; and at
   degree $P$ the theory **descends** to the first layer of a smaller order of the same family — an
   equality that complex conjugation, not a formal argument, is what pins down.

## 📦 What is here

| | |
|---|---|
| `conductor_rho_line.pdf`, `conductor_rho_line_es.pdf` | the note, English and Spanish, as deposited |
| `conductor_rho_line.tex`, `conductor_rho_line_es.tex`, `fig_*.pdf`, `figuras.py` | the sources and the figure script |
| everything else | 137 files: the scripts behind every number labelled *measured* or *observed*, and their archived output |

`README.md` in the ancillary archive maps each number of the note to the script that produces it and
to the file that holds its run. A script `foo.sage` or `foo.py` writes `foo_OUT.txt` beside it.

## 🧪 How to doubt a number

Find the script named after the statement, read its header — each says what it computes and how to
run it — and either read the `*_OUT.txt` beside it or run it again. The `.sage` files run under
SageMath 10.x; everything else is Python 3 with `numpy`, `sympy`, `matplotlib`, and `pymupdf` for the
one gate that measures the rendered page.

Several gates carry a **control that must fail**: the half-period sweep runs 12 cases with $p\mid B$,
where the prediction is expected to break and does; the factor at $2$ has near-miss controls with
$p\mid h^-$; the general-$\ell$ rank statement carries seven controls at $p=2$, two of which fail, and
that is why the statement says *odd* $p$.

## 🚫 What is deliberately not here

The correspondence around this line of work does not travel with it. It is held out **by location,
not by a list of names** — a name list cannot see what is inside a file, and excluding one by name
leaves the references to it dangling in what does ship. A check refuses to release a bundle in which
anything imports or reads a file that is not in it; this bundle passes it.
